## Goal

As a maintainer, I want every rework-verdict test converted into a real
observable-behaviour assertion, so the suite keeps its coverage while losing its
dead weight.

## Context

This is the largest child in the epic. The planning-time probe flagged 55 of 431
tracked test files; the dominant class is source-grep (a test reads a source or
markdown file and asserts on its text), followed by placeholder/zero-assertion and
self-referential simulation cases.

**Decided** (producer delegated, recorded on `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`): this
repository deliberately carries tests that read files — 181 tracked test files
reference a `.md` path, ~127 read one. They are **not** one class, so "reads a
markdown file" is not a defect. Every in-scope file that touches `.md` is tagged
with one of five classes, and only the last two are rework/prune candidates:

| Class | What it is | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **A — sandbox fixture** | the test creates/edits `README.md`, `notes.md` etc. inside a temp repo to exercise production code | out of scope; `.md` is incidental (≈104 files) |
| **B — production output** | production code writes the `.md` (changelog, audit report, standup, churn report) and the test asserts the artefact | out of scope; keep (≈22 files) |
| **C — link/structure hygiene** | parses markdown to assert links resolve, referenced paths exist, required headings are present | keep; must parse structure, never match prose |
| **D — doc-contract** | asserts a document *states* a rule or invariant (e.g. the finish-gate semantics in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`) | **rework** to parsed structure |
| **E — duplicate convention grep** | a narrow per-skill text grep whose convention is already covered generically (e.g. `tests/unit/test-triage-skill.mjs` vs `tests/test_skill_path_conventions.py`) | **prune** |

Class D rule: assert parsed structure (headings, frontmatter keys, labelled
bullets, table cells, parsed links) or, where the exact wording *is* the
contract — a sentence an agent is told to quote — cite in a comment the work item
that mandates that wording. Class D must not assert raw prose substrings.

## Deliverables

- Reworked test files/cases (behaviour assertions in place of text/structural
  assertions).
- Detector corrections in `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` where the
  evaluator is demonstrably wrong about a sound test, each with a regression test.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Work the `rework` verdict set from the Classify child, batched by area
   (`tests/`, `skill/audit`, `skill/implement`, `skill/shared`, `skill/test`,
   `skill/standup`, node `.mjs`), one child work item per area batch once the
   list exceeds ~25 files.
2. For each reworked case: identify the observable behaviour the source text was
   standing in for (emitted event, returned value, state transition, CLI exit
   code, rendered node, parsed document structure) and assert **that**; write the
   failing assertion first where the behaviour is already implemented so the test
   is proven able to fail.
3. Where the behaviour is genuinely unobservable, hand the case back to `prune`
   (with an evidence note) rather than inventing an assertion.
4. Where the evaluator is a false positive, fix the detector (keeping it
   conservative) and add a regression test in
   `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_usefulness.py`; never delete a sound test to
   silence the tool.
5. Re-run `evaluate_usefulness.py` over the touched area after each batch and
   record the `remove`-count drop.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_usefulness.py`
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`
- `tests/**/test_*.py`, `skill/*/tests/test_*.py`, `tests/unit/*.mjs` (targets)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All `rework`-verdict tests are converted to observable-behaviour assertions; no remaining test file reads a source/markdown file and asserts on its text in class D (doc-contract prose) or class E (duplicate convention grep); classes A (sandbox fixture), B (production output) and C (link/structure hygiene) are explicitly exempt.
- [ ] Every in-scope file that touches a `.md` path is tagged with its file-usage class (A–E) in the classification artefact, and only class D and E files are reworked or pruned — no class A, B or C file is modified by this item.
- [ ] Class D files assert parsed structure, or cite the work-item id that mandates the exact wording when the wording itself is the contract.
- [ ] After the refactor, `evaluate_usefulness.py` reports no `remove` verdict for any scanned test file, and the suite contains zero placeholder or zero-assertion tests.
- [ ] Every reworked case is demonstrably able to fail: the behaviour-asserting test was observed red against a deliberately broken/mutated behaviour (or written assertion-first) before landing.
- [ ] Evaluator false positives are fixed in the detector with a regression test rather than by deleting or weakening a sound test, and each fix is recorded in the completion comment.
- [ ] Work is split into area batches when the list exceeds ~25 files, each batch green (changed scope during work, full scope before the item closes) and each batch's completion comment recording the `remove`-count drop.

## Constraints & assumptions

- No coverage-maximisation: a reworked test that asserts less but observes real
  behaviour is a success; a reworked test that asserts more text is not.
- Follow `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` when choosing the replacement
  assertion.
- Decision (recorded on the epic): repository-contract/inventory tests survive in
  parsed-structure form rather than being deleted wholesale; the five-class
  taxonomy above is closed for this pass, and a sixth class discovered mid-work
  is added to `test-writing-guidelines.md` with an example rather than handled
  ad hoc.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — parent epic (AC4, AC5).
- `SA-0MWG5115X005MEIM` — Prove (prerequisite).
- `SA-0MWG51CGK004RNOK` — prune remediation (complementary).
- `SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23` — the 5 known source-grep tests (separate item; exclude).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer behaviour over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the suite itself to reject a new anti-pattern test, so the
pruned classes cannot silently return.

## Context

`skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` already classifies a test file as
`remove` when it finds a source-grep, placeholder, zero-assertion, self-referential
or duplicate-coverage pattern. What is missing is a **standing gate**: nothing runs
the evaluator over the suite, so nothing stops a new offender being added. This
child adds that gate — as a test, in test-first style, and without itself becoming
the anti-pattern it screens for.

## Deliverables

- A suite-level guard test that fails when an in-scope test file is dirty, built on
  the shared evaluator API rather than duplicated regexes.
- A documented, work-item-required exemption mechanism that must be empty at
  completion of this epic.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the guard as a test (for example `tests/test_test_value_guard.py`) that
   enumerates in-scope test files exactly as the Measure baseline does (tracked
   files only; `.worklog/worktrees/**` excluded) and calls
   `evaluate_usefulness.evaluate_file` on each, failing with a per-file report
   when any verdict is `remove` or the file contains a placeholder/zero-assertion
   case.
2. Feed the guard two fixture sets so it is proven able to fail: a clean fixture
   (passes) and an offender fixture (fails with a useful message). Do not assert on
   the guard's own source text.
3. Add a bounded, class-aware exemption mechanism: a checked-in list of
   `{path, class, work-item-id}` entries that suppresses a specific file, where
   `class` is one of the file-usage classes decided on the epic (A sandbox
   fixture, B production output, C link/structure hygiene). The list must be
   empty when this epic closes; a class D or E file may never be exempted. A test
   asserts every exemption cites a live work item and a valid class.
4. Wire the guard into the existing suite (no new runner, no new skill) and
   measure its overhead; document it in `skill/test/SKILL.md`.
5. Keep the run bounded: the static scan of ~430 files is expected to stay well
   under five seconds; if it does not, cache the verdicts by file content hash.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_test_value_guard.py` (new)
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`
- `skill/test/SKILL.md`
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`
- `.pi/test-config.json` (only if a group wiring change is needed)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A regression guard fails the suite if a newly added test matches a pruned anti-pattern class (source-grep, placeholder, zero-assertion, self-referential simulation), without becoming a source-grep test itself.
- [ ] The guard is built on the shared evaluator API (single source of truth for the anti-pattern rules) and is proven able to fail by clean/offender fixtures.
- [ ] Every exemption to the guard cites a work item id and a file-usage class (A/B/C) in a checked-in list that is tested to reference live items; class D and E files can never be exempted, and the list is empty when the epic closes.
- [ ] The guard does not flag the ≈104 class A fixture tests or the ≈22 class B production-output tests that read or write markdown, demonstrated by fixtures for each class.
- [ ] The guard adds no new runner or skill, is documented in `skill/test/SKILL.md`, and its measured overhead is recorded (target: under five seconds on the current in-scope set).

## Constraints & assumptions

- Test-first: the guard's offender fixture must be shown red before the guard is
  accepted green.
- The guard scans **test files**, not production source: asserting on the guard's own
  or production source text would violate the very rule it enforces.
- Scope set is derived, never hardcoded per area, so new test directories are
  covered automatically.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — parent epic (AC8).
- `SA-0MWG50OB2003ON99` — Classify: the anti-pattern set the guard enforces (prerequisite).
- `SA-0MWG51CGK004RNOK`, `SA-0MWG51S1D0084L0H` — remediation, so the guard lands on a clean suite.
- `SA-0MWG52KSC008DFKC` — documentation learnings.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the pruning workflow and anti-pattern guidance to carry
what this pass learned, so the next suite-wide review starts from better criteria.

## Context

The workflow lives in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` (pruning review workflow) and the
anti-pattern catalogue in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` (7 classes:
source-grep, placeholder, self-referential simulation, duplicate coverage,
type-level/structural-only, zero-assertion browser/scene, real-git without sandbox).
This pass is expected to surface at least two new refinements:

1. **File-level false positives** — the evaluator returns `remove` for a file with
   one offending case, so a verdict is never authority to delete a file.
2. **File-reading tests are not one class** — 181 tracked test files reference a
   `.md` path and ~127 read one, but only two of the five classes are defects. The
   guidelines must publish the closed taxonomy (A sandbox fixture, B production
   output, C link/structure hygiene, D doc-contract, E duplicate convention grep)
   with a real example per class, so "reads a markdown file" is never treated as a
   defect on its own.

## Deliverables

- Updated `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`: new/refined anti-pattern
  classes, each with a real example from this pass, the fix applied, and the
  exemption rule.
- Updated `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` pruning workflow: the measure → classify →
  prove → remediate → guard loop as executed here, with the evidence bar for a
  deletion.
- Updated `skill/test/SKILL.md` covering the evaluator batch mode and the guard.

## Minimal Implementation

1. After remediation and the guard land, replay the pass's findings against the
   two documents and add the refinements (with repo examples and file pointers).
2. State the deletion evidence bar explicitly: no removal without an evidence
   entry resolving the candidate REMOVE.
3. Document the exemption class and how a new exemption is added (work item id
   required) so the guard and the guidance cannot drift apart.
4. Keep the prose UK English and preserve existing headings/anchors that other
   tests or skills link to.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`
- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md`
- `skill/test/SKILL.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The pruning workflow in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` and the anti-patterns in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` are updated with anything this pass learned (new anti-patterns, refined criteria).
- [ ] Each new or refined class carries a real example from this repository, the fix applied, and the evidence bar for deletion — not generic advice.
- [ ] `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` publishes the closed five-class file-usage taxonomy (A fixture, B production output, C link/structure hygiene, D doc-contract, E duplicate convention grep) with one real example per class, and states the class D rule (parsed structure, or a work-item citation when the exact wording is the contract).
- [ ] `skill/test/SKILL.md` documents the evaluator's batch mode and the regression guard, cross-linking both documents and the guard's class-aware exemption rule.
- [ ] UK English throughout, existing links/anchors preserved, and the repository's documentation/link tests pass.

## Constraints & assumptions

- Documentation-only change: no behaviour change to any skill.
- The guidance must remain conservative: an ambiguous case stays `keep` and is
  filed as a work item, never silently reclassified as removable.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — parent epic (AC9).
- `SA-0MWG50OB2003ON99` — Classify: source of the anti-pattern adjudications.
- `SA-0MWG5284K004J1YN` — the guard whose exemption rule this documents.
- `SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC` — churn metrics in the refactor skill.

## Goal

As a producer, I want the before/after deltas recorded and signed off, so the value
delivered by this epic is auditable.

## Context

Everything before this child produces evidence; this child reconciles it into one
report and confirms the epic's acceptance criteria are met. Without it the epic's
"prove the value" premise is unverified.

## Deliverables

- [ ] AC1: The markdown "Yesterday I completed work on..." section is split into two labelled sub-groups, auto-dispatched first then manual, each with a plain-language heading (TTS-friendly): "Work auto-dispatched by the downtime worker" and "Work I dispatched myself".

- [ ] AC4: TTS output (yesterday_tts renders) speaks the split in first person, e.g. "Yesterday the downtime worker completed..." / "I completed..."; no IDs, backticks, or ISO timestamps in spoken lines. The auto/manual *_tts arrays carry the same per-item impact-first sentences as yesterday_tts.

- [ ] AC5: Grouping does not change item ordering inside a group (keep updatedAt then id sort) or yesterday_count.

Integrate the test-churn analyser into the refactor pipeline as an additional, non-fatal stage after smell detection, for both full-project and session-boundary modes, surfaced in the human report and `--json` output, with a `--no-churn` escape hatch and runtime (subprocess) resolution of the analyser.

## Goal

Update `select_group_from_changed_files` to return `frozenset[str] | None` instead of `str | None`, representing the union of **all** groups whose `paths` match at least one changed file. The iteration order must be deterministic (sorted group names).

## Problem

Currently `select_group_from_changed_files` returns a single group via `min()` — when multiple groups match a changed file, only one is returned. This causes the changed-scope gate to skip testing all other affected skill suites (SA-0MVEJIHIG003WTH9).

## Requirements

- Return `frozenset[str] | None` (sorted group names in the frozenset for determinism).
- All groups whose `paths` spec matches **any** changed file are included.
- Single-group match returns a frozenset with one element (backwards-compatible with callers that check `bool(result)`).
- `None` when no groups match (unchanged fallback).
- Deterministic: iteration order is sorted group names, not set-iteration order.
- `full` group is still intentionally excluded from selection.

## Impact

A cross-skill change set (e.g. touching implement + test + audit skills) now surfaces all affected groups, enabling the changed-scope gate to test every one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Changes to `skill/implement/**`, `skill/test/**`, and `skill/audit/**` returns `frozenset({"implement", "test", "audit"})`.
- AC2: A single-group change returns `frozenset({"audit"})` (single element).
- AC3: No matching files returns `None` (unchanged fallback).
- AC4: `full` group is never included in the returned frozenset.
- AC5: Existing single-match tests in `TestChangedFileToGroup` are updated to expect frozenset returns.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `select_group_from_changed_files` (line ~1614)
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_groups.py` — `TestChangedFileToGroup` tests

## Dependencies

- None — this is the foundational change that other children depend on.

## Goal

Update `changed_scope_selection` to iterate all matched groups (from the new multi-group `select_group_from_changed_files`), union their commands, and check outside-group files against the union of all matched groups\’s `paths`.

## Problem

`changed_scope_selection` currently calls `select_group_from_changed_files` which returns a single group, then computes outside-group files only relative to that one group. When multiple groups match, only the first groupsquo;s outside files are checked, and the otherssquo; test files are silently dropped.

## Requirements

- `ChangedScopeSelection.group` changes from `str | None` to `frozenset[str] | None`.
- `changed_scope_selection` iterates all groups in the frozenset and unions their commands.
- `_changed_outside_group_paths` is updated (or a multi-group variant added) to check changed files outside the **union** of all matched groups\’s `paths`.

## Goal

As a build agent, I want failing-first regression tests that pin the environment-bound cache contract, so the implementation in the sibling children cannot silently keep serving a drifted-worktree verdict to a canonical-checkout consumer.

## Background

Parent SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L (producer decisions Q1c / Q2a / Q3a). Today the cache key is `normalized command + git fingerprint (+ test_type namespace)` only; `store()` records just `interpreter` as environment provenance, so an entry recorded in a worktree with an unpopulated submodule, a differently-resolved `node_modules`, or a different interpreter is key-identical to a canonical-checkout run of the same tree. These tests are written **first** (TDD): they fail against `dev` HEAD and must pass once `skill/test_cache.py` folds a coarse environment fingerprint into the key.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests in `tests/test_test_cache.py` (new cases, existing fixture style) fail against today's environment-blind key and pass once the environment fingerprint is keyed: (a) an entry stored under a drifted environment fingerprint is a **miss** for a lookup carrying the canonical environment fingerprint — the verdict is never served; (b) two checkouts with **equivalent** environments share one cache entry (same submodule completeness, same installed `node_modules` state — a symlinked `node_modules` pointing at an identical install counts as equivalent — same interpreter); (c) identical environment state in two different absolute directories yields the **same** environment fingerprint (path-independence).
- Tests assert every stored entry records `environment_fingerprint` plus a human-readable descriptor of its components (submodule status, `node_modules` resolution state, interpreter), and that `lookup()` rejects an entry that predates the field (fail closed — never environment-blind green).
- Tests assert the environment fingerprint is deterministic (two successive computations on an unchanged checkout are byte-identical) and cheap: a spy/monkeypatch proves no recursive `node_modules` walk and at most one `git submodule status` call per computation.
- Existing cache provenance tests (`fingerprint_kind`, `scope`, `test_type`, `interpreter`) keep passing unchanged, and the whole file stays hermetic (temporary git repos, no network, no dependence on the host's installed packages).
- Parent AC6 restated — Regression tests in `tests/` where the cache layer and gates are tested: (a) drift-keyed entries are never served to a canonical-environment consumer — the canonical lookup misses and executes; (b) equivalent-environment entries still share across checkouts (finish gate ↔ pre-push ↔ audit); (c) the escalation path runs `--scope changed --force` for narrow changes and `--scope full --force` on detected drift/refactor; (d) existing cache provenance tests stay green. (This child delivers the cache-layer half (a), (b), (d); the gate-path case is delivered by `run_tests env-aware cache keys and gate provenance`, the escalation case (c) by `finish: escalate post-push verification in canonical env`, and the cross-consumer case (b) end-to-end by `Cross-consumer env-key equivalence and audit evidence notes`; this child owns the failing-first tests those children make pass.)

## Minimal implementation

- Add the new cases to `tests/test_test_cache.py` against the intended API (`compute_environment_state(cwd)`, `cache_key(..., environment_fingerprint=...)`, `store(..., environment=...)`, `lookup(..., environment_fingerprint=...)`).
- Use temporary git repositories plus a synthetic `node_modules/.package-lock.json` marker so drift/equivalence are simulated without touching the real checkout.
- Mark the drift/equivalence cases to fail cleanly (no import error masquerading as a pass) while the primitive does not yet exist.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/test_test_cache.py`
- `skill/test_cache.py` (test target only — no production change in this child)

## Dependencies

- None (first child; every implementation child depends on it).

## Notes / assumptions

- TDD ordering is deliberate: this child lands the failing tests, `test_cache environment fingerprint and provenance` makes them pass.

data.description:
## Goal

As a build agent, I want the pre-push hook to stop copying a drifted-worktree gate entry into the main checkout's cache, so main-checkout consumers are never handed an entry that claims canonical-environment evidence it does not have.

## Background

Parent SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L (AC5). `.githooks/pre-push`'s `mirror_suite_cache()` copies every entry the gate's worktree cache holds into `<main>/.worklog/cache` on the assumption "an identical key is an identical run". With the environment fingerprint folded into the key, an equivalent-environment entry is already key-identical and safe to mirror; a drift-keyed entry is a different key and pollutes the canonical cache. Depends on the environment fingerprint primitive and the runner wiring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `mirror_suite_cache()` compares each candidate entry's recorded `environment_fingerprint` with the canonical (main checkout) environment fingerprint computed via the shared helper, and **skips** entries that do not match, emitting an explicit notice such as `pre-push: skipped cache entry <key> (environment drift)`; matching entries are mirrored exactly as today.
- The mirror step stays fail-soft: a helper/git failure never fails the hook and never mirrors an entry whose environment cannot be verified — it skips with a notice instead.
- A regression test drives the hook's mirror step against (a) a drift-keyed entry → not copied, (b) an equivalent-environment entry → copied, (c) an unverifiable entry → skipped with a notice; the test exercises the shipped hook logic rather than a re-implementation.
- `.githooks/pre-push`'s comment and the "Cache compatibility" section of `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` state that an identical key now means identical git state **and** equivalent environment.
- Parent AC5 restated — Each entry records the environment fingerprint (and its component descriptor: submodule status, `node_modules` resolution, interpreter) as provenance metadata alongside `fingerprint_kind`/`interpreter`; the pre-push mirroring either skips entries whose environment fingerprint cannot be matched to the canonical environment or records them so consumers can reject them. Documented in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9 and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (exact escalation commands, when a forced full run is required vs a targeted one), with audit skill F3/F4 notes where relevant. (This child delivers the mirroring half; the provenance metadata is delivered by `test_cache environment fingerprint and provenance`, and the documentation halves by `finish: escalate post-push verification in canonical env` and `Cross-consumer env-key equivalence and audit evidence notes`.)

## Minimal implementation

- In `.githooks/pre-push`, add a small Python helper invocation (repo-local `skill/test_cache.py` first, installed global-skill copy as fallback, mirroring the existing `gate_reason` tiering) that computes the canonical fingerprint and checks each entry's `metadata.json`.
- Print a stderr notice per skipped entry; never `exit` non-zero.
- Extend `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py` (or add `tests/test_pre_push_cache_mirror_env.py`) with a temporary main checkout + worktree cache fixture.

**Key Files:**

- `.githooks/pre-push`
- `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py`
- `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`

## Dependencies

## Background

## Goal

As a producer, I want a before/after behaviour-coverage map, so I can see that the
refactor removed waste rather than coverage.

## Context

Epic AC6 requires that no acceptance criterion of any work item loses coverage,
demonstrated by the audits and a **before/after coverage map** — explicitly not by
assertion counts or coverage percentages. The Remediate children delete and rework
tests; this child proves the behavioural net effect.

## Deliverables

- `docs/dev/test-value-coverage-map.md` — before/after map: behaviour → surviving
  test (or documented "not observable").
- A cited full-suite run (test skill, full scope) evidencing a green tree.

## Minimal Implementation

1. From the Prove evidence and the remediation comments, build a table of every
   behaviour pinned by each removed or reworked test, and the surviving test (path
   + test name) that now covers it; use "not observable / target gone" with the
   evidence link where no survivor exists.
2. Group the table by area (skills, release/ship, test infrastructure, wl/worklog,
   docs contracts) so reviewers can skim.
3. Cross-check the map against the epic's AC list and the child ACs, marking any
   behaviour that has no survivor as a gap requiring a follow-up work item.
4. Run the full suite through the test skill and cite the cached run in the
   document (no ad-hoc test invocations).

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/test-value-coverage-map.md`
- `docs/dev/test-value-evidence.md`
- `docs/dev/test-value-classification.json`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The suite is green (full scope, run via the test skill) and no acceptance criterion of any work item loses coverage — demonstrated by the audits and a before/after coverage map, not by assertion counts.
- [ ] A before/after behaviour-coverage map records, for every removed or reworked test, the behaviour it pinned and the surviving test that covers it, or a documented "not observable" with its evidence link.
- [ ] The suite is green at the point of verification, demonstrated by a cited full-scope run through the test skill (cached run id/commit recorded).
- [ ] Any behaviour found without a survivor is either restored (test re-added) or filed as a follow-up work item referenced from the map — none is left unaccounted for.
- [ ] The map is organised by area and cross-checked against the epic and child acceptance criteria, so a reviewer can confirm no acceptance criterion lost coverage without counting assertions.

# TypeScript/JavaScript Parser Adapters

## Goal
Implement parser adapters that extract assertion patterns, mock usage, and test structure from TypeScript/JavaScript test files.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Per-file reporting matching parent AC** — Parse .test.ts, .spec.ts, .test.js, .spec.js files and report per file: total assertion count, count of assertions on internal collaborators vs public/behaviour, mock/stub/spy instantiation count and ratio, and number of test cases with no meaningful assertion.
2. **File discovery** — Identify .test.ts, .spec.ts, .test.js, .spec.js files within a given directory tree (respecting node_modules exclusion).
3. **Assertion extraction and classification** — Detect and count all assertion patterns:
   - Jest/Vitest: expect(...).toBe, expect(...).toEqual, expect(...).toMatch, etc.
   - Jest mock call-arguments: toHaveBeenCalledWith, toHaveBeenNthCalledWith
   - Python-style (future-proof but not implemented in v1): assert_called_once_with
4. **Mock/stub/spy detection** — Detect mock instantiation patterns:
   - jest.fn(), jest.spyOn(), vi.fn(), vi.spyOn()
   - mock(), stub(), spy() (generic patterns)
   - Import-based detection: import { mock, stub } from ...
5. **Test case boundary detection** — Identify test function boundaries (test(...), it(...), describe(... nesting)).
6. **Zero-assertion test detection** — Flag test cases that have no meaningful assertion within their body.
7. **Tests** — Unit tests with mock file content covering all patterns.

## Constraints
- Static analysis only — no test execution.
- Conservative: uncertain patterns are flagged, not discarded.
- Language-neutral entry point; TypeScript/JavaScript is v1.

## Key Files
- `skill/test/scripts/assertion_quality_analyser/typescript_adapter.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_typescript_adapter.py`

# Core Analysis Engine — Mock Density and Assertion Quality

## Goal
Implement the core analysis logic that computes mock density and assertion quality scores from parsed test data.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mock density calculation** — Compute the ratio of mock/stub/spy usage relative to total assertions:
   - Count mock instantiations (jest.fn, vi.spyOn, etc.)
   - Count mock assertions (toHaveBeenCalledWith, toHaveBeenNthCalledWith, assert_called_once_with, mock.call_args_list)
   - Compute mock-to-assertion ratio
   - Flag files exceeding the configurable mock density threshold
2. **Assertion quality scoring** — Compute a quality score based on:
   - Proportion of call-argument assertions (mock method calls) vs behaviour assertions (return values, state changes)
   - Ratio of weak assertions (toBeDefined, toBeTruthy) to strong assertions (toEqual, toMatchObject)
   - Flag tests with no meaningful assertion
3. **Mock-call flagging on internal collaborators** — Assertions on toHaveBeenCalledWith, toHaveBeenNthCalledWith, assert_called_once_with, and mock.call_args_list on internal collaborators (mocks injected in test setup, not production return values) are reported as a distinct, actionable signal. Public/behaviour assertions (on return values of production function calls) are reported separately. Aligned with SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G calibration rules.
4. **Uncertainty flagging** — When the analyser cannot confidently classify an assertion type (e.g., dynamic expect targets, helper function assertions), flag the uncertainty rather than producing a false classification.
5. **Configurable thresholds** — All thresholds (mock density, weak assertion ratio) are configurable constants with documented rationale and sensible defaults.
6. **Tests** — Unit tests covering all calculation paths, threshold boundaries, and uncertainty scenarios.

## Constraints
- Conservative: never auto-flag or auto-prune based on scores.
- Scores are proxy signals, not ground truth.
- Align with calibration rules from SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G.

## Key Files
- `skill/test/scripts/assertion_quality_analyser/analysis_engine.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_analysis_engine.py`

## Goal

Define, before any implementation exists, the exact loader contract the
test-value aggregator must satisfy: how each upstream analyser's output is
read, normalised, and recorded as **present**, **absent** or **malformed**.

## Target outcome

A synthetic fixture set representing every upstream signal (plus its real
schema) and a failing-then-passing `test_loaders.py` that pins the contract.
This is the test-first half of the evidence-ingestion slice.

## Definition of done

- `skill/test-value/tests/fixtures/` holds minimal, hand-written JSON for:
  churn (`test_churn_data.json` shape: `metadata.analyser_version`,
  `file_stability.top_files[]` with `file`/`commits`/`total_additions`/
  `total_deletions`/`area`), mutation (`mutation_report.json` +
  `suite_source_map.json` planned shape), anti-pattern (per-file
  `{"file","verdict","reasons","summary"}` from
  `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py --json`), and optional
  runtime/flake data.
- Fixtures also cover the absent cases (file missing) and malformed cases
  (unknown schema version, non-JSON, missing required keys).
- `tests/test_loaders.py` fails (ImportError) until the loaders land, then
  passes. It asserts the three-way signal status, not "silently empty".
- No fixture embeds real repository paths; all are relative and portable.

## Constraints

- Read-only against any analysed project; fixtures must not shell out.
- Fixture schemas mirror the current upstream output exactly; a schema change
  upstream must show up as a deliberate fixture edit, not silent inference.
- Do not import the upstream analysers to *generate* fixtures — hand-written
  fixtures keep the aggregator's contract decoupled from upstream internals.

## Risky assumptions

- The mutation schema (`mutation_report.json`, `suite_source_map.json`) is
  planned by `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` and not yet landed, so the fixture encodes
  *the documented plan*, not observed output. If the landed schema differs the
  fixture is updated as a deliberate change (documented in the item).
- The churn per-file signal only covers `file_stability.top_files` (top 20
  feature-commit-churned files), so "absent" is the common case for most test
  files — the contract must model that explicitly rather than infer churn 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fixtures exist for churn, mutation, anti-pattern and runtime signals, plus absent and malformed variants of each.
- `test_loaders.py` asserts present/absent/malformed status for every signal type.
- `test_loaders.py` asserts malformed input surfaces an explicit loader error naming the signal and reason — never a silent empty result.
- `test_loaders.py` asserts relative-path normalisation and deterministic ordering of loaded per-file records.
- `test_loaders.py` asserts loading does not recompute any churn, mutation or anti-pattern metric (values flow through unchanged).

## Key Files

- `skill/test-value/tests/conftest.py` — Loads the aggregator modules by path and exposes fixture paths.
- `skill/test-value/tests/fixtures/churn_data.json` — Synthetic churn analyser output.
- `skill/test-value/tests/fixtures/mutation_report.json` — Synthetic mutation report (planned schema).
- `skill/test-value/tests/fixtures/suite_source_map.json` — Synthetic suite→source map.
- `skill/test-value/tests/fixtures/anti_pattern.json` — Synthetic `evaluate_usefulness.py --json` output.
- `skill/test-value/tests/test_loaders.py` — Loader contract tests (present/absent/malformed/deterministic).

## Dependencies

None — this is the first test-first item. Blocks the loader implementation.

## Goal

Implement `loaders.py`: thin adapters that read each upstream analyser's JSON
output and return a normalised, three-state signal (`present` / `absent` /
`malformed`) per test file — without recomputing any upstream metric.

## Target outcome

The evidence-ingestion vertical slice lands: given an artefact path, the
aggregator knows exactly what evidence exists, what is missing and why, and
never infers a value it was not given.

## Definition of done

- `load_churn`, `load_mutation`, `load_anti_pattern`, `load_runtime` each
  return `Signal(status, per_file, reason, source_metadata)`.
- `source_metadata` preserves the upstream `analyser_version` / `generated_at`
  for the report's "pinned inputs" section.
- A missing file → `absent` with a reason string. A present-but-unreadable or
  schema-drifted file → `raised loader error` naming signal + reason (never a
  silent empty payload).
- Path normalisation to repo-relative POSIX form; deterministic ordering.
- `tests/test_loaders.py` (created by the sibling test item) passes unchanged.

## Constraints

- No git calls, no parsing of test source, no metric recomputation — loaders
  are pure readers. Anti-pattern classification stays in
  `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`; mutation scoring stays in
  `skill/mutation-test/`.
- Churn per-file evidence is limited to `file_stability.top_files`; a file
  absent from that list is reported as `absent` (not churn 0).
- Mutation is `absent` while `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` has not landed — this is
  the expected, honest state.
- No per-project hardcoded paths; every loader takes an explicit path.

## Risky assumptions

- The planned mutation schema may shift when its arm lands; the loader
  validates a declared `schema_version` and fails loudly on an unknown one
  rather than guessing.
- `suite_source_map.json` attribution is suite→module, so a test file inherits
  the score of every module it maps to; the loader records the mapping as-is
  and leaves the aggregation policy to the decision model.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Ingests, per test file, churn metrics (rewrite/growth/stability), mutation score, anti-pattern verdicts and runtime/flake data when available, recording each as present, absent or malformed.
- Each loader records `present`, `absent` or raises an explicit loader error, and never returns an empty payload for a malformed input.
- Loader output is path-normalised to repo-relative POSIX form and deterministically ordered.
- No loader invokes git, parses test source, or recomputes churn/mutation/anti-pattern metrics.
- Upstream analyser version/`generated_at` metadata is carried through for the report's pinned-inputs section.
- The sibling loader-contract tests (`test_loaders.py`) pass.

## Key Files

- `skill/test-value/scripts/loaders.py` — Upstream artefact readers and normalised signal type.
- `skill/test-value/tests/test_loaders.py` — Contract tests this item must satisfy.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the loader contract test item (test-first).

## Goal

Exercise the aggregator against this repository's real signals and record the
resulting register, proving honest degradation in practice (mutation and
runtime absent, churn partial) rather than only in synthetic tests.

## Target outcome

A documented, reproducible validation run: the command executed, the artefact
paths, the verdict totals, the absent-signal list, and a spot-check of three
files whose evidence is compared against the raw upstream analyser output.

## Definition of done

- Run the churn analyser once to produce a real `test_churn_data.json`, and the
  anti-pattern evaluator over the in-scope files, then run the aggregator in
  consume mode against those artefacts.
- Attach a summary to this work item: command line, totals (keep/rework/prune
  and `insufficient_evidence`), absent signals, and the top of the register.
- Spot-check ≥ 3 files (one per verdict class where possible): the report's
  cited evidence must match the raw analyser values, or the discrepancy is
  filed as a defect child on the aggregator item.
- Confirm `prune` recommendations (if any) each cite ≥ 2 corroborating
  signals and are presented as advisory.
- Record whether mutation evidence was available at run time; if
  `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` has not landed, state that the register is a
  partial-signal register by design.

## Constraints

- Artefacts are written to a temp/output directory, not committed (they are
  run outputs, not source).
- Do not delete or move any test file as part of this validation — `prune` is
  advisory and remediation belongs to the epic's separate Remediate items.
- Do not run the agent-initiated test suite directly; any suite run goes
  through `/skill:test`.
- Runtime cost bounded: restrict the anti-pattern pass to the in-scope set and
  record the wall-clock.

## Risky assumptions

- A real run will show many `insufficient`-evidence and `rework` verdicts
  because churn is top-20 only and mutation is absent; that outcome is the
  honest result, not a failure of the aggregator.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documented command is executed against this repository and the resulting verdict totals and absent-signal list are recorded on this item.
- At least three files are spot-checked and their cited evidence is confirmed to match the raw upstream analyser values.
- Every `prune` recommendation in the run is confirmed to cite at least two corroborating signals and to be presented as advisory.
- The run records whether mutation and runtime signals were available, and states explicitly when the register is partial-signal by design.

# Modify merge-dev-to-main.sh: JSON capture + classification

## Problem
The release gate (`merge-dev-to-main.sh`) runs `run_tests.py` without `--json`, so every failure — red suite, slot contention, killed run — produces the same "Full test suite failed" message. The operator cannot tell "fix the code" from "wait for a slot / raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`", and a release attempt can burn hours of queue wait before failing indistinguishably from a real regression.

## Solution
Mirror the pre-push hook pattern (SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI):

1. Run `python3 "$TEST_RUNNER" --json --scope full --strict-git-env` and capture stdout to a temp file.
2. Resolve the classifier via the same tiered search (repo-local `skill/test/scripts/`, then `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/`).
3. Run an inline Python script (heredoc) that:
   - Imports `classify_gate_result` and `render_gate_diagnostic` from `gate_reason`.
   - Reads the JSON output file and classifies the failure.
   - Falls back to `gate_reason=infrastructure` if the classifier is unavailable.
   - Prints `render_gate_diagnostic(reason, result)`.
4. Print the diagnostic to stderr, then exit non-zero on failure (as the hook does).

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1 — The release gate runs `run_tests.py --json --scope full --strict-git-env`, captures stdout to a temp file, and classifies the result through the shared `gate_reason` classifier (repo-local tier first, then `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/`). On failure it prints a `gate_reason=<code>` line and a human-readable diagnostic from `render_gate_diagnostic()`.
- AC2 — Distinct messages for contention/killed vs red suite: a slot-contention or killed-run failure prints a distinct message with the remediation hint (wait then re-run, or raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`), while a red suite keeps the "Full test suite failed" message with its own remediation.
- AC3 — Fails closed in every failure case; `SHIP_TEST_SKIP=1` still bypasses: the gate exits non-zero on every failure path (slot contention, timeout, killed, test failure, unparsed, infrastructure, unknown), and `SHIP_TEST_SKIP=1` bypasses the gate entirely, as it does today.
- AC4 — The inline classifier resolves via tiered search (repo-local `skill/test/scripts/` first, then `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/`) and falls back to `gate_reason=infrastructure` when unavailable (never fail-open).
- AC5 — On success the gate prints "Release gate: full suite green".

## Constraints
- UK English.
- Do not duplicate classification logic; consume `gate_reason.py` only.
- Follow the pre-push hook pattern exactly.
- The gate must remain hermetically testable (the existing test fixture pattern must continue to work).

## Key Files
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — the full-suite gate block.
- `skill/test/scripts/gate_reason.py` — the shared classifier (read-only dependency).

## Dependencies
- Blocked by the classification test slice (`SA-0MWIT2QNH000RYCD`): the tests are written first (red), and this slice makes them green.

# Add classification tests: JSON-emitting fake runner

## Problem
The existing gate tests (`tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py`) use a fake runner that only records invocations and returns an exit code. They cannot exercise the JSON classification path, so nothing pins the new `gate_reason` behaviour.

## Solution
Extend the test fixture in `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` with a JSON-emitting fake runner that produces structured results matching `run_tests.py`'s `--json` output shape, and assert that `merge-dev-to-main.sh` classifies each correctly.

### Test cases
- **Green suite**: runner emits `{"failures": [], "exit_code": 0}` → gate prints "full suite green" and exits 0.
- **Test failure**: runner emits `{"failures": [{"name": "test_foo"}], "exit_code": 1}` → gate prints `gate_reason=test_failure`, exits non-zero.
- **Slot contention**: runner emits `{"notice_codes": ["slot_busy"], "failures": [], "exit_code": 1}` → gate prints `gate_reason=slot_contention` with the wait-then-retry / raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` hint, exits non-zero.
- **Killed run**: runner emits `{"notice_codes": ["killed"], "failures": [], "exit_code": 1}` → gate prints `gate_reason=killed`, exits non-zero.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1 — Hermetic test pins the classification: a test in `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` (or a new test file) exercises the classifier against a fake runner that produces JSON results for slot contention, killed, and red-suite cases, asserting the correct `gate_reason` and diagnostic output.
- AC2 — Green-suite case: runner emits success JSON → the gate prints "Release gate: full suite green" and exits 0.
- AC3 — Test-failure case: runner emits structured failures → the gate prints `gate_reason=test_failure` and the red-suite remediation, exits non-zero, creates no PR.
- AC4 — Slot-contention case: runner emits a `slot_busy` notice → the gate prints `gate_reason=slot_contention` with the wait-then-retry / raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` hint, exits non-zero.
- AC5 — Killed-run case: runner emits a `killed` notice → the gate prints `gate_reason=killed` with the killed remediation, exits non-zero.

## Constraints
- UK English.
- Reuse the existing test fixture pattern (`_build_release_fixture`, `_run_release`) — isolated `HOME`, fake runner, fake `gh`.
- No ad-hoc suite invocations; the tests are hermetic and run through the test skill.
- Written first (expected red) against the modified `merge-dev-to-main.sh`.

## Key Files
- `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` — new classification test cases go here.
- `skill/test/scripts/gate_reason.py` — the classifier under test.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — the modified script under test.

## Dependencies
- None. Blocks the implementation slice (`SA-0MWIT20V9004VBR6`): the tests are written first (red) and the implementation makes them green.

# End-to-end Python detection pipeline

Deliver a working, runnable near-duplicate detector for Python test files: AST extraction, normalisation, shingle/Jaccard similarity, inverted index, basic clustering, CLI, and JSON + Markdown output. This is the tracer-bullet slice — it goes from test-file collection through to written reports in one deliverable.

## Parent AC coverage

This task covers **AC1 (structural detection)** — Python test blocks detected via ast with docstrings stripped, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders, literals canonicalised to type placeholders so a renamed copy still matches; never raw text equality. Also covers **AC2 (clusters reported with location and score)** for the Python path — each cluster lists member file paths, start-end line ranges, block sizes, similarity scores and redundancy measure; JSON + Markdown written to --output-dir. Also covers **AC4 (performance bounds)** — inverted shingle index used instead of all-pairs; --min-lines, --threshold defaults.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 - Detection is structural, not textual. Near-duplicate test blocks are detected within and across files using normalised representation: Python test blocks via ast (docstrings stripped, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders, literals canonicalised to type placeholders so a renamed copy still matches), JavaScript/TypeScript/other test files via comment-stripped token normalisation with brace-matched block boundaries. Raw text equality is never the similarity measure. (This slice delivers the Python part; JS/TS follows in the next slice.)
- AC2 - Clusters are reported with location and score. Each cluster lists every member's file path, start-end line range, block size (lines and tokens), member-to-member and cluster similarity score, and a redundancy measure (member lines minus the largest member's lines) used to order the report. Both test_duplicates.json (versioned schema: thresholds, method, limitations, clusters) and test_duplicate_report.md (human, same content, ordered by redundancy) are written to --output-dir. (This slice delivers the Python path end-to-end.)
- AC3 - Python block extraction: top-level functions, classes, methods, and with-wrapped test bodies are extracted with file path and start-end line range.
- AC4 - Python normalisation: docstrings removed, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders per lexical scope, literals canonicalised to type placeholders (string to {str}, int to {int}, etc.), whitespace collapsed.
- AC5 - Token k-gram shingle generation (k default 5), Jaccard similarity, and inverted shingle index producing candidate pairs without all-pairs O(n^2) comparison.
- AC6 - Basic transitive clustering of blocks above threshold, redundancy measure (member lines minus largest member lines), clusters ordered by total redundant lines descending.
- AC7 - CLI accepts: --project-root, --output-dir, --min-lines N, --threshold, and --quiet. Shaped like the churn analyser CLI.
- AC8 - test_duplicate_report.md and test_duplicates.json written with method, thresholds, limitations and cluster data; one-line summary printed to stderr.
- AC9 - Output is deterministic: same tree and flags produce byte-identical JSON; non-deterministic sources (file system order) are sorted.
- AC10 - Unit tests cover: Python AST extraction of async tests, parametrised tests and nested classes; normalisation invariance (renamed copy scores >= threshold); distinct behaviour below band; shingle and Jaccard behaviour; inverted index correctness; basic clustering and redundant-line arithmetic; JSON and Markdown schema/content; deterministic output; empty/single-block suite.
- AC11 - skill/test-churn/SKILL.md gains a Near-duplicate detection section and docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md gains a skeleton recording the method and thresholds; both updated in this slice, not deferred.

## Deliverables

- skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py - Python extraction, normalisation, shingling, Jaccard, inverted index, basic clustering, CLI, JSON/MD writers
- skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_duplicate_detection.py - unit + e2e tests for the Python pipeline
- skill/test-churn/tests/conftest.py - path-loaded fixture for test_duplicate_detection
- skill/test-churn/SKILL.md - Near-duplicate detection section
- docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md - method and thresholds skeleton

## Key Files

- skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py - extract_blocks_python(), normalise_python_ast(), generate_shingles(), jaccard_similarity(), build_inverted_index(), cluster_blocks(), write_json_report(), write_md_report(), main()

# Classification, conservatism and JS/TS support

Add the conservative classification layer (similarity bands, expected-repetition detection) and multi-language support (JS/TS token extraction) to the working Python pipeline. This slice turns the basic detector into one that refuses false positives and understands non-Python tests.

## Parent AC coverage

This task covers **AC1 (structural detection)** for JS/TS — comment-stripped token normalisation with brace-matched block boundaries, no raw text equality. Also covers **AC3 (conservatism and legitimate repetition)** in full — pytest.mark.parametrize, unittest.subTest, test.each/it.each, data loops classified expected-repetition; explicit similarity bands (duplicate >= threshold default 0.85, near-duplicate >= lower band default 0.65); report-only verdict on every cluster; tool never edits, deletes or renames anything. Also refines **AC2 (clusters reported)** — member-to-member and cluster similarity scores, redundancy measure used to order the report.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 - Detection is structural, not textual. Near-duplicate test blocks are detected within and across files using normalised representation: Python test blocks via ast (docstrings stripped, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders, literals canonicalised to type placeholders so a renamed copy still matches), JavaScript/TypeScript/other test files via comment-stripped token normalisation with brace-matched block boundaries. Raw text equality is never the similarity measure. (This slice adds the JS/TS and other-language part.)
- AC2 - Conservatism and legitimate repetition. Parametrised/table-driven repetition is classified expected-repetition, not redundancy: pytest.mark.parametrize, unittest.subTest, test.each/it.each, and blocks whose sweep is a data loop over case literals are detected and excluded. Similarity bands are explicit (duplicate >= threshold, default 0.85; near-duplicate between the lower band, default 0.65, and the threshold), every cluster carries a report-only verdict, and the tool never edits, deletes or renames anything.
- AC3 - Clusters are reported with location and score. Each cluster lists every member's file path, start-end line range, block size (lines and tokens), member-to-member and cluster similarity score, and a redundancy measure (member lines minus the largest member's lines) used to order the report. Both test_duplicates.json (versioned schema: thresholds, method, limitations, clusters) and test_duplicate_report.md (human, same content, ordered by redundancy) are written to --output-dir. (This slice adds member-to-member and cluster similarity scores and the full classification fields.)
- AC4 - JS/TS block extraction: comment-stripped tokenisation with brace/paren matching identifies function and class body boundaries; unparseable blocks are reported as unparsed in the JSON summary rather than silently compared as a whole file.
- AC5 - JS/TS normalisation: comment removal, identifier renaming, literal canonicalisation applied to token stream.
- AC6 - Expected-repetition detection covers pytest.mark.parametrize, unittest.subTest, test.each/it.each, and data loops over case literals; these clusters are excluded from redundancy totals.
- AC7 - Similarity bands are explicit: duplicate >= threshold (default 0.85), near-duplicate >= lower band (default 0.65) and < threshold; below band is not a match; --near-duplicate-threshold configurable.
- AC8 - Every cluster carries a verdict of report-only; the tool never edits, deletes or renames any file.
- AC9 - Unit tests cover: JS/TS token extraction of arrow functions and class methods; non-Python file set; expected-repetition detection for pytest.mark.parametrize, unittest.subTest, test.each and data loops; similarity band boundaries (0.85, 0.65, below 0.65); report-only verdict; unparsed-block reporting.

## Goal

When the audit accepts a cached verdict as full-suite evidence, report its `fingerprint_kind` (tree or worktree) and age in the audit output so a reused verdict is visible rather than implied.

## Implementation

1. Extend `_classify_full_suite_cache`'s return so the accepted evidence carries the `fingerprint_kind` that served it and the entry age (seconds from `completed_at`). Update EVERY existing unpack site: `_auto_green_run_outcome`, `_resolve_auto_green_run`, plus the tests that unpack the tuple (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_green_run.py`, `skill/test/tests/test_hidden_skill_tests.py`).

2. Propagate the fingerprint kind and age through `_auto_green_run_outcome` to its caller (`cmd_issue`'s automatic-verification path) and into the persisted report.

3. Extend the persisted report's evidence line (currently `Automatic green run evidence: <sha> (cached full-suite run)`) to name the key kind and age, e.g. `Automatic green run evidence: <sha> (cached full-suite run, tree-keyed, 42s old)`.

4. Include the same facts in the injected AUTO-VERIFIED GREEN RUN block so Phase 1/2 models are told the verdict was reused, not freshly executed.

## Acceptance criteria

- The reused verdict's `fingerprint_kind` and age are reported in the audit output/JSON (persisted report evidence line and the injected prompt block), e.g. `cached full-suite run, tree-keyed, 42s old`.
- A reused tree-kind verdict is labelled `tree-keyed`; a reused worktree-kind verdict is labelled `worktree-keyed`.
- Age is displayed in a human-readable form.
- Every existing unpack site of the classifier's return value is updated, and no caller silently drops the new fields.

## Key files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_classify_full_suite_cache`, `_auto_green_run_outcome`, `_auto_green_run_prompt_block`, `_resolve_auto_green_run`, the persisted-report evidence lines

## Impact

An operator reading audit output can immediately see whether the evidence was tree-keyed or worktree-keyed, and how old it is.

## Tests to write

1. **Tree-kind hit (no execution):** Prime the cache with a tree-keyed entry at the HEAD tree SHA. Run `_classify_full_suite_cache` and assert GREEN without executing any command (no `run_cached` / `run_all` call). Assert `fingerprint_kind="tree"` in the result.

2. **Legacy worktree hit:** Prime the cache with a worktree-keyed entry at the exact HEAD worktree fingerprint. Run `_classify_full_suite_cache` and assert GREEN. Assert `fingerprint_kind="worktree"` in the result.

3. **Different-tree miss:** Prime the cache with a tree-keyed entry for a *different* tree SHA (not the current HEAD tree). Run `_classify_full_suite_cache` and assert MISS.

4. **Unchanged `query_cached` default:** Verify that `query_cached()` called without `fingerprint`/`fingerprint_kind` still defaults to the worktree-keyed lookup, preserving the existing contract for other callers. A tree entry never satisfies a worktree request.

5. **Tree-kind reported with age:** Verify that when a tree-kind entry is accepted, the `fingerprint_kind` and age are reported (the persisted evidence line / prompt block), e.g. `tree-keyed, 42s old`.

## Test file

Add the cases to the existing audit full-suite cache home, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_green_run.py`, or a sibling module in `skill/audit/tests/` (e.g. `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_full_suite_cache_tree.py`). Reuse the `_default_green_full_suite_cache` fixture in `skill/audit/tests/conftest.py`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Deterministic tests cover: tree-kind hit (no execution), legacy worktree hit, different-tree miss, and the unchanged `query_cached()` default for other callers.
- The tree-kind hit test asserts the suite is NOT executed and that tree-keyed evidence is accepted.
- The reused verdict's `fingerprint_kind` and age are asserted in the reported output.
- Tests are deterministic and do not depend on the real cache directory or live git state (mock `query_cached` / prime a tmp cache).
- Every new behaviour is exercised by an automated test executed through the test skill, and the full suite passes.

## Key files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_classify_full_suite_cache`, `_auto_green_run_outcome`
- `skill/audit/tests/conftest.py` — `_default_green_full_suite_cache` fixture pattern
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_green_run.py` — existing audit runner cache tests
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` — existing tree-keyed cache test patterns to mirror

## Impact

Deterministic test coverage for the tree-kind cache evidence path.

# RCA: ship writes that invalidate audits

## Summary

Document the exact ship/release close-path writes that move `updatedAt` past `auditedAt` on released items, the freshness rule that then reports them stale, and the intended-or-avoidable decision with the at-fault layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- RCA documented: identifies the exact ship/release steps that move `updatedAt` on released items (the `wl close --force --reason "Shipped in vX"`, `wl update --status completed --stage done`, `wl comment add` and producer-review override write types, with their call sites in `run-release.js`) and the exact freshness rule that then reports them stale, with representative item ids and timestamps as evidence, classifying the affected audits as v2 content-fresh (protected by the probe) versus legacy/manual (time-gate only).
- Records the exact freshness rule that reports those items stale (`isAuditStale` in `skill/ship/scripts/audit-freshness.js` and `_check_audit_freshness` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`), including the 60 s time gate and the 30 s persistence tolerance.
- Provides representative evidence with item ids and timestamps (audited vs updated vs closed) — e.g. SA-0MWE1EAR30045VHO (v2 content match) and SA-0MWE4BT63005N8OE (manual legacy) — plus store-wide classification counts: v2 content-fresh (protected by the probe) versus legacy/manual (time-gate only).
- States the decision — intended or avoidable — per audit class, with justification tied to the existing content-freshness contract (SA-0MVTU2643004QTQN), and names the at-fault layer (release write path, freshness rule, or display/dispatcher consumer).
- Records the RCA write-up and decision on SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G (comment plus changelog block) before the dependent items begin.

## Minimal Implementation

- Read the release close path in `run-release.js` (close/cascade/comment writers, ~lines 700-735 plus overrides), the freshness gate in `audit-freshness.js`, `check-audit-gate.js` and `refresh-audits.js`, and the runner's `_check_audit_freshness` in `audit_runner.py`.

- Classify the stale set (v2-verified vs legacy/manual) and determine per-class validity of the invalidation.
- Write the decision into the item, including the recommended fix boundary when avoidable.

RCA write-up with evidence and the intended-or-avoidable decision recorded on the parent work item.

# Stop ship invalidating unchanged audits

## Summary

Implement the RCA-directed minimal change so a ship run no longer leaves content-unchanged (v2-verified) audits reading as out of date after the close/re-stage writes — without re-running the audit pipeline for the backlog, without weakening verdict semantics, and without regressing the SA-0MUOO5TRU005ALBL stale-audit false-block fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Implements the minimal change so that a ship run does not leave content-unchanged audits reading as out of date — preserving the audit freshness signal through the close/re-stage write (e.g. a truthful content fingerprint of the final description) — **without** re-running the expensive audit pipeline for the backlog and without weakening verdict semantics.
- The content-fresh fast path (`hasContentFingerprint` / `queryContentFreshness` / `attemptAuditRemediation`) and the child-reuse gate are preserved; `--force` still bypasses the gate.
- No mass re-audit: the audit pipeline is not fanned across the in-review/backlog set; read-only probes stay read-only (no test-suite execution or pi calls from the freshness probe).
- Legacy/manual audits (no v2 line) resolve per the RCA decision: either the smallest truthful mechanism (applied only when content-unchanged can be verified) or the documented intended side effect, with any display-only consumer (herdr, separate repository) filed as a linked item rather than edited here.
- Any freshness metadata written at close is truthful (fingerprint of the final description; original `auditedAt` and verdict preserved) — never fabricated.
- The stale-audit false-block regression tests (SA-0MUOO5TRU005ALBL) and the F2 freshness tests pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Apply the RCA-recommended change: content-aware classification in `planAuditRefresh` / the stale-flag consumers and/or a truthful close-path freshness-signal preservation in the `run-release.js` close/cascade/comment writes (or the runner's persistence helpers).
- Keep every probe read-only and bounded; introduce no lifecycle `wl` writes beyond the existing close path.

## Deliverables

Minimal production change with the F2 tests green; description updated per the F1 RCA decision before implementation begins.

   of its metric's definition (AC2).

## Goal

Write the targeted tests for SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1 AC4: the producer-review flag rule 'only when the audit failed for any reason, or code/content changed since the last review' — and the ship-triggered carve-out boundary where a passing re-audit of unchanged work never sets the flag, a failing re-audit (independent or ship-triggered) always does, and a content-change signal is never swallowed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests exercise production code (`_resolve_producer_review_decision` / `_passing_audit_producer_decision` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`), not re-implementations of it.
- Passing unchanged re-audit (top-level 'Yes', reviewed, same fingerprint) → no `--needs-producer-review` write: independent run resolves `preserved`, ship-triggered run resolves `untouched`.
- Never-reviewed passing re-audit → independent run resolves `required` (today's failsafe, unchanged); ship-triggered run resolves `untouched` (the shipped SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ behaviour is retained: neither AC1 branch — audit failed / content changed since the last review — holds for a verification pass with no prior review baseline).
- Failed re-audit (top-level 'No') independent → `required`, and `--needs-producer-review yes` is written.
- Failed ship-triggered re-audit (top-level 'No') → still `required` / `--needs-producer-review yes` (SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1 AC2 boundary — the divergence from SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ AC1 resolved in this item's favour).
- Content change (prior passing audit whose stored fingerprint differs from the current one) with the ship-triggered marker and a top-level 'Yes' → `required` (AC3 — the marker never swallows the fingerprint change signal, "exactly as an independent audit would").
- Ship-triggered marker absent → today's independent-flag semantics preserved exactly (preserved/required/untouched per SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST, SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42).
- No test asserts that a flag is ever *cleared* (`--needs-producer-review no`): suppression means no write.

rationale: A 62.3% read error rate indicates speculative path guessing. Existence checks, clearer not-found diagnostics, and guidance to anchor paths to skill_path or detected roots would reduce retries.
evidence_sessions: 2026-11-16T14-54-27-990Z_herdr-1794840867-4024106-29197.jsonl, 2026-11-16T16-03-37-574Z_herdr-1794845016-4166175-9322.jsonl

## Summary

Make path discipline an explicit agent rule: anchor every path to a resolved root and
check existence before reading, instead of guessing a path and retrying on not-found.

## Problem

Log review records a 62.3% `read` error rate: agents construct plausible paths
(`skill/x/...`, `docs/y.md`, worktree paths) that do not exist, then retry with
variations. The `read` tool is provided by the pi harness, so the in-repo lever is
guidance plus a diagnostic checklist, not tool code.

## Users

- AI agents: need a rule and a recipe that make the first read attempt land.
- Maintainers: need the shared rule in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`, where every project inherits it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Agent guidance requires a preflight existence check and root-relative paths before reading a file.
  - `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` gains a "Path discipline for file reads" rule: resolve the root first (`skill_path` for skill files, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` for repository files, the worktree root for implementation edits), then check existence with `test -e`/`ls`/`git ls-files` before reading a guessed path.
- `docs/dev/path-discipline.md` documents the anchoring recipes (main checkout, linked worktree, installed skill directory), a not-found diagnostic checklist and two worked examples taken from the 2026-11-16..17 sessions.
- The plan, implement and audit skill docs reference the new section instead of restating it, so there is one canonical rule.
- `tests/test_agents_global_path_discipline.py` asserts the rule text and the doc cross-links exist, in the style of `tests/test_agents_global_stages.py`.
- The harness half is recorded explicitly: either a linked upstream work item requesting a preflight/not-found hint in the `read` tool, or the accepted rationale for guidance-only.
- No local behavioural change to the `read` tool itself.

## Minimal Implementation

- Tests first: `tests/test_agents_global_path_discipline.py` (rule present, no duplicate rule blocks, links resolve).
- Add the "Path discipline for file reads" rule to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` next to the existing worktree-isolation invariant.
- Write `docs/dev/path-discipline.md` with the recipes, the not-found checklist and the worked examples.
- Add one-line references in `skill/plan/SKILL.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `skill/audit/SKILL.md` file-access guidance.
- Record the upstream decision in the doc and, if a harness change is wanted, create the linked follow-up item (do not edit `.pi/` or the harness here).

## Key Files

- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`
- `docs/dev/path-discipline.md` (new)
- `tests/test_agents_global_path_discipline.py` (new)
- `tests/test_agents_global_stages.py` (pattern to mirror)
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`

## Dependencies

- None. Documentation-only slice; pairs with `SA-0MWJYSZAP001PCN8` (which supplies the `roots` command the rule points at) but does not block on it.

## Risks and assumptions

- Assumption: the harness `read` tool cannot be changed from this repository, so the in-repo deliverable is guidance plus docs; this is recorded as an honest limitation, not hidden.
- Risk: another `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` rule section risks duplication with the worktree-isolation invariant; the new section must cross-reference it rather than restate it.
- Risk: doc-only changes can rot; the doc-hygiene test is what keeps the rule and links alive.

## Deliverables

- New global rule, `docs/dev/path-discipline.md`, skill cross-references and a doc-hygiene test.
- A recorded decision on the upstream `read`-tool half.

## Impact

Agents stop burning retries on invented paths: they resolve the root, check once, and read the file that actually exists on the first attempt.

target_skill: implement
impact_scope: global
priority_hint: medium
rationale: Push rejection led to stash pop conflicts, checkout/restore attempts, and merge conflicts. A guided recovery path should avoid destructive cleanup and report exact dirty/staged/stash/conflict state.
evidence_sessions: 2026-11-16T14-54-27-990Z_herdr-1794840867-4024106-29197.jsonl

## Summary

Add a read-only recovery diagnosis to `implement.py finish` that reports the exact
repository state and the safe next actions when a push, stash pop or merge goes wrong.

## Problem

A rejected push in the review window led to stash-pop conflicts, `checkout`/`restore`
attempts and merge conflicts, with agents guessing which tree and which stash was
involved. `implement.py` already detects orphaned stashes at `start`, but nothing helps
an agent diagnose a wedged `finish` without reaching for destructive cleanup.

## Users

- AI agents stuck in a failed `finish`: need a diagnosis and a safe, explicit next step.
- Producers: need assurance that recovery never destroys uncommitted work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `implement.py finish` offers a safe git recovery mode that reports dirty, staged, stash and conflict state without destructive cleanup.
  - `finish --recover` reports the resolved repo root, worktree root, branch, upstream, dirty and staged paths, stash entries (with any work-item ids found in them), in-progress merge/rebase/cherry-pick state and conflict paths.
- `--recover` reports dirty, staged, stash and conflict state without destructive cleanup: it exits 0 with the diagnosis and a proposed action list, and never runs `git stash drop`, `git reset --hard`, `git checkout --force` or worktree removal.
- When the pre-push gate or the push fails, `finish` prints the exact `implement.py finish --recover` command for the resolved worktree root instead of leaving the agent to guess.
- Tests assert the diagnosis payload keys and that no destructive git command is ever issued in recovery mode.
- The recovery playbook in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` documents the mode and its non-destructive guarantee.

## Minimal Implementation

- Tests first: `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_recover_diagnosis.py` (payload keys, conflict/merge-state detection) and `test_finish_recover_never_destructive.py` (command allow-list assertion).
- Add `--recover` to `finish` argument parsing and a diagnosis helper reusing `git_stash_list` and `_extract_work_item_ids_from_stash`, plus existing status/merge-state helpers.
- Wire the push-failure and gate-failure paths to print the recovery command with the resolved root.
- Keep recovery strictly read-only: no commits, no stash mutation, no worktree operations.
- Document the mode, its guarantees and the suggested action order in the two reference docs.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_finish`, `git_stash_list`, `_extract_work_item_ids_from_stash`, `check_orphaned_stashes`, `parse_args`)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_recover_diagnosis.py` (new)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_recover_never_destructive.py` (new)
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `SA-0MWJYSZAP001PCN8` (canonical worktree root): the diagnosis must report the resolved roots rather than re-guess them.

## Risks and assumptions

- Assumption: read-only diagnosis plus an explicit action list is enough to unblock agents; automated repair is out of scope and would violate the never-destructive guarantee.
- Risk: reporting stash entries may expose work from other items on the shared ref; the diagnosis must name ids rather than dump diffs.
- Relationship: the existing orphaned-stash warning at `start` stays as is; this item adds the diagnosis to `finish`.

## Deliverables

- `--recover` diagnosis in `finish` with a non-destructive guarantee and tests.
- Push/gate failure messages that point at the recovery command.

## Impact

A failed push or stash pop stops turning into destructive guesswork: agents see the exact repository state and a safe next step, and uncommitted work survives recovery.

## Summary

Pin down the `run_tests.py --json` result contract and add a single fast iteration
shorthand, so agents stop re-parsing an undocumented payload and stop reaching for
full-suite runs during implementation.

## Problem

Log review shows full runs that exceeded the per-command timeout, followed by broad
re-runs with longer timeouts, then repeated parsing of the JSON result to work out what
failed. `--scope changed`, `--group` and `--list-groups` already exist
(`SA-0MUJKF2HP001BR51`), but the fast path is not the obvious default for iteration and
the JSON payload has no documented, versioned contract.

## Users

- AI agents iterating in implement sessions: need a fast command and a stable payload.
- The finish gate, audit cache and triage tools: need a contract that cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `run_tests.py` documents a stable JSON result schema and offers a fast scoped default: a `--fast` shorthand selects changed scope plus the unit profile, while explicit `--scope`/`--type` still win and the existing changed-scope fallback to full is preserved.
- The `--json` payload carries `schema_version` and keeps its keys additive-only, with the documented contract covering `success`, `suites`, `failures`, `discarded_failures`, `notices`, `notice_codes`, `resolution_notices`, `scope`, `type`, `resolved_scopes` and the new `failure_summary`.
- `failure_summary` gives per-suite failure counts plus the first N failure titles, so an agent can triage without re-reading `stdout`.
- Each `failures[]` entry has stable keys (`suite`, `test`, `file`, `line`, `message`) documented field by field.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` documents the contract, the fast-iteration recipe and the consumer mapping (implement finish gate, audit cache, triage), and a test asserts the documented keys and the emitted keys cannot drift.
- The default `--scope full` behaviour, the audit-accepted full-suite cache and the release gate are unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

- Tests first: `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_json_schema.py` (schema_version, required keys, failure entry keys, doc/emitter parity) and `test_run_tests_fast_scope.py` (`--fast` selects changed+unit, explicit flags win, fallback to full preserved).
- Add `schema_version` and `failure_summary` to the result dict assembled in `run_tests.py`, keeping every change additive.
- Add `--fast` to the argument parser and apply it only when `--scope`/`--type` were not supplied.
- Document the contract, the fast-iteration recipe and the consumer mapping in `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`.
